title: The four consumed owner operations of the writ step are named by no source and the plan carries no contract dependency for either slice
source: 04 User stories/Recovery Workbench User Stories Epics 3 to 8 v3.md (heading RWB-E5-018, its Endpoints and Permission checks tables); Recovery Workbench FSD S4 Litigation and enforcement v3 (A2.18.2 Integration points, A2.18.3.3); Recovery Workbench TSD S4 Litigation and enforcement v2 (T2, T5.1, T5.2, T5.3, appendix T-A.1); _work/msr/context/S4.md (ownership rows of S4: two tables, five REST operations, zero events, zero jobs, one workflow); _work/msr/plan/split_plan.json (both slices of RWB-E5-018, the C, I and X lists empty)
section: APP s2 Business rationale; s3 Preconditions; s4 Flow steps 8 and 9; s10 Authority; s12.2; s12.4; s12.8; s13 Solution plan; s19 Out of scope; CON s2, s3, s7 AC3 and AC4, s11 Data, s12.2, s12.8, s13
description: The writ step cannot run without four facts of other owners: the case route state ENFORCEMENT_DECISION and the enforcement decision of rwb-case (P3), the case-move answer WRIT_AND_SEIZURE of the same owner, the instruction of the panel firm of rwb-partner (S9), and the LITIGATION rule package with R-LIT-54 of rwb-decision (P7). No source read for this key names any of the four operations: the TSD S4 T5.2 names only the modules (P3 for the case, P7 for the decision log, P4 for access and reference data, P5 for documents, P6 for notices), appendix T-A.1 lists the five operations this service provides and none it consumes, and T5.3 declares no event. The plan carries an empty C list, an empty I list and an empty X list for both slices, so the metadata rows read None although the four facts are class C dependencies in fact. Both stories therefore build against the published documents of their owners and against fakes on Day 1, every consumed row carries the placeholder of section R9, and the absence is recorded rather than filled with an invented operation name.
evidence: TSD S4 T5.2 reads: Calls go through the published Java interfaces: P3 for the case, P7 for the decision log, P4 for access and reference data, P5 for documents, P6 for notices. TSD S4 T5.3 gives the event table as None. TSD S4 appendix T-A.1 lists API-S4-001 to API-S4-005 as provided operations only. _work/msr/context/S4.md gives the ownership rows as 2 tables, 5 REST operations provided, 0 events, 0 jobs and 1 workflow. split_plan.json gives C, I and X as empty lists for RWB-S4-E5018-APP and RWB-S4-E5018-CON. FSD S4 A2.18.2 names the integration points as Partner portal and LIT only, and names no case or rule operation.
owner_role: S4 rwb-litigation service owner with the P3 rwb-case, S9 rwb-partner and P7 rwb-decision owners
proposed: Step D1 decides whether the four consumed rows become class C dependencies of both slices and the owners publish operation names; until then the stories build against the documents and fakes of the four owners.

title: The legacy key carries no requirement id in the story master and the plan carries no requirement for either slice
source: 04 User stories/Recovery Workbench User Stories Epics 3 to 8 v3.md (heading RWB-E5-018, its metadata table with no Requirement row); _work/msr/plan/split_plan.json (the reqs list of both slices, empty); Recovery Workbench FSD S4 Litigation and enforcement v3 (Requirements served, REQ-S4-007); Recovery Workbench TSD S4 Litigation and enforcement v2 (T8)
section: APP s2 Business rationale; s18 Traceability; the reqs key of both fragments; CON s18 Traceability
description: The traceability of the two stories needs one sourced requirement. The legacy story master of RWB-E5-018 carries no requirement id, the plan's reqs list for both slices is empty, and TSD S4 T8 lists REQ-S4-001 to REQ-S4-010 against FEAT-LIT-01 only, with Written one epic ahead in the story column. The only requirement of the module that names the outcome of the writ step is REQ-S4-007, Enforcement after judgment has one named owner from judgment to the end of enforcement, which is what AC1 and AC2 ask when the firm is instructed and the case moves to WRIT_AND_SEIZURE. Both stories therefore trace to REQ-S4-007 and the empty plan list is recorded rather than filled with an identifier no owner approved.
evidence: The metadata table of RWB-E5-018 gives Epic, Module, Feature, Process, Priority, Depends on and Decision only, with Depends on as FEAT-LIT-17. The plan rows of RWB-S4-E5018-APP and RWB-S4-E5018-CON carry reqs as an empty list. FSD S4 Requirements served gives REQ-S4-007 Enforcement after judgment has one named owner from judgment to the end of enforcement. TSD S4 T8 lists ten requirements against FEAT-LIT-01 only.
owner_role: S4 rwb-litigation service owner with the business analyst
proposed: Trace both slices to REQ-S4-007 and let step D1 update the plan reqs list of the two slices to that identifier.

title: LOV-LEGAL-TYPE names no writ value and legal_action carries no writ, seizure or deadline column
source: Recovery Workbench TSD S4 Litigation and enforcement v2 (T3.1 DF-LEG-001 to DF-LEG-014, T3.2 LOV-LEGAL-TYPE and LOV-LEGAL-STATUS); Recovery Workbench FSD S4 Litigation and enforcement v3 (A2.18.3.1, A2.18.3.2 field catalog); Recovery Workbench Business Rules and Routing Logic v4 (R-LIT-54); 04 User stories/Recovery Workbench User Stories Epics 3 to 8 v3.md (heading RWB-E5-018, its Data, Endpoints and Screen and states tables)
section: APP s1 Story; s2 Business rationale; s3 Preconditions; s8 BR4; s11 Data; s12.7; s13 Solution plan; s15 Screens and states; s17 Guardrails; CON s2, s7 AC1 and AC6, s11 Data, s13, s17
description: The feature is a writ and a seizure and the data model has no name for either. LOV-LEGAL-TYPE gives NOTICE, CIVIL_CASE, APPEAL, ENFORCEMENT, BANKRUPTCY_PETITION and LED_AUCTION and no writ value, legal_action gives id, case_id, law_firm_id, action_type, lawsuit_no, black_case_no, red_case_no, court_name, claim_amount, filed_date, judgment_date, judgment_amount, lit_status and status (DF-LEG-001 to DF-LEG-014) and no seizure date, no enforcement step and no deadline, and the legacy Data table names only the recovery_case, decision_log_entry and rule_row rows of the monolith. The writ is therefore carried as the enforcement type of the list, the court facts of the writ are carried on the existing court reference columns, the writ deadline is carried as a durable timer with a reference value, and no column is added by either story.
evidence: TSD S4 T3.2 gives LOV-LEGAL-TYPE as NOTICE, CIVIL_CASE, APPEAL, ENFORCEMENT, BANKRUPTCY_PETITION, LED_AUCTION and LOV-LEGAL-STATUS as OPEN, FILED, JUDGMENT, ENFORCING, CLOSED, WITHDRAWN. TSD S4 T3.1 lists DF-LEG-001 to DF-LEG-014 with no writ or seizure field. FSD S4 A2.18.3.2 lists the eight operated fields of the feature and none is a writ or seizure field. R-LIT-54 gives the action as Instruct the firm to apply for the writ and seizure with the timer To the writ deadline.
owner_role: S4 rwb-litigation service owner with the data steward
proposed: Apply the writ as action_type ENFORCEMENT and keep the writ and the seizure as facts of the action and of the decision record; if a writ or seizure column is later required, raise it as an additive migration on the DB story of S4.

title: The FSD S4 and the TSD S4 that both slices read are In review with an empty sign-off table and the realigned stories have no approval
source: Recovery Workbench FSD S4 Litigation and enforcement v3 (document control, document sign-off); Recovery Workbench TSD S4 Litigation and enforcement v2 (document control, document sign-off); Recovery Workbench Epics 3 to 8 Specification v3 (status); Template and Rules v1 R8.1; AGENTS.md rules 9 and 10
section: Metadata row Status of both stories; APP s3 Preconditions; CON s3 Preconditions
description: The sources of both slices are not approved. The FSD S4 is at version 3 in review with an empty sign-off table and the TSD S4 is at version 2 in review with an empty sign-off table, and the run of D-RCV-60 has no human approval step, so the missing approval is recorded as an assumption, both stories carry Status Draft (realignment v1) and the work continues. No behaviour and no value of either story depends on a signature, and no status of a source document is changed.
evidence: FSD S4 document control gives Status In review and its document sign-off table has empty Name, Signature and Date cells; TSD S4 v2 document control gives Status In review and its sign-off table is empty; Template and Rules v1 R8.1 asks every new document for a change-log row naming D-RCV-60 and the tool line; AGENTS.md rule 9 says a missing approval is recorded as an assumption and the work continues in Draft.
owner_role: Solution architect and the business owner of S4
proposed: Keep both stories at Draft (realignment v1) and let the verification loop collect the sign-offs before any status changes.

title: The writ deadline of R-LIT-54 has no interval in any source and the story carries it as a reference value
source: Recovery Workbench Business Rules and Routing Logic v4 (R-LIT-54, timer column); Recovery Workbench FSD S4 Litigation and enforcement v3 (A2.18.3.1); Recovery Workbench TSD S4 Litigation and enforcement v2 (T4); Recovery Workbench Temporal and Drools Design Text Extract v1 (S4 litigation slide, prescription clock); 04 User stories/Recovery Workbench User Stories Epics 3 to 8 v3.md (heading RWB-E5-018, AC2)
section: APP s2 Business rationale; s4 Flow step 9; s8 BR6; s12.6; s13 Solution plan; s17 Guardrails; CON s2, s3, s7 AC5, s12.6, s19
description: R-LIT-54 instructs the firm to apply for the writ and seizure with the service level To the writ deadline, and no source gives the length of that deadline: the rule workbook gives the label only, the FSD A2.18 gives no interval, TSD S4 T4 reproduces the rule row, and the Temporal and Drools extract ties the litigation clock to the prescription date of the case rather than to the writ. Both stories therefore carry the deadline as one durable timer of LitigationWorkflow whose length is a versioned reference value, declare no timer row and no Schedule, and mark the value with the placeholder of section R9 instead of inventing a number of days or months.
evidence: Business Rules and Routing Logic v4 row R-LIT-54 gives the timer as To the writ deadline. FSD S4 A2.18.3.1 gives VR-S4-018-1, R-LIT-54 and BR-S4-018 and no interval. TSD S4 T4 lists R-LIT-01 to R-LIT-25 and 54 more and gives no interval for the writ. The Temporal and Drools extract states that the prescription clock never pauses and gives no writ deadline value.
area: Rules and reference data, S4 rwb-litigation
owner_role: Business owner of the LITIGATION route set in rwb-decision with the reference-data owner
proposed: Add the writ deadline as a versioned reference row owned with the LITIGATION package and read by the timer; no code constant is created.

title: The case route state, the traced asset and the economic test that R-LIT-54 turns on have no home in this service
source: _work/msr/context/S4.md (ownership rows of S4: two tables, legal_action and hearing); Recovery Workbench TSD S4 Litigation and enforcement v2 (T3.1, T3.3, T4, T5.2); Recovery Workbench FSD S4 Litigation and enforcement v3 (A2.18.1 metric, A2.18.3.1); Recovery Workbench Business Rules and Routing Logic v4 (R-LIT-50, R-LIT-52, R-LIT-53, R-LIT-54); 04 User stories/Recovery Workbench User Stories Epics 3 to 8 v3.md (heading RWB-E5-018, its Data table and Screen and states table)
section: APP s1 Story; s2 Business rationale; s3 Preconditions; s4 Flow steps 1, 4 and 9; s8 BR3 and BR5; s9 State transitions; s11 Data; s12.7; s19 Out of scope; CON s2, s7 AC3 and AC4, s11 Data, s12.7, s19
description: R-LIT-54 fires from ENFORCEMENT_DECISION on ENFORCE_APPROVED only when an asset is traced and enforcement is economic, and neither fact belongs to this service. The case and its route state are rwb-case's (recovery_case is a P3 row and TSD S4 T5.2 sends the case to P3), the traced asset is the outcome of R-LIT-50 to R-LIT-53 and of RWB-S4-E5017-APP, and legal_action carries no asset reference: DF-LEG-001 to DF-LEG-014 give no asset, no valuation and no economic test field. The legacy story could read recovery_case and the asset in one schema; the target cannot. Both stories therefore announce the move WRIT_AND_SEIZURE to rwb-case instead of writing a case row, read the traced asset and the economic test as inputs of the rule package, and record that no asset reference is added to this service's schema.
evidence: _work/msr/context/S4.md gives the S4 tables as hearing and legal_action only. TSD S4 T5.2 sends the case to P3. TSD S4 T3.1 gives legal_action no asset, valuation or economic field. Business Rules and Routing Logic v4 gives R-LIT-50 (ASSET_TRACE, 10 working days), R-LIT-52 (ASSETS_FOUND to ENFORCEMENT_DECISION) and R-LIT-54 (the condition an asset is traced and enforcement is economic). The legacy Data table names recovery_case as a row of the story.
owner_role: S4 rwb-litigation service owner with the P3 rwb-case owner and the owner of RWB-S4-E5017-APP
proposed: Keep the case and the route state with rwb-case and the traced asset with RWB-S4-E5017-APP and the rule package, and record any asset reference as a later additive change if the asset-trace story needs one.

title: The legacy Endpoints table names two operations while the flow of the feature and TSD appendix T-A.1 need a third, the update
source: 04 User stories/Recovery Workbench User Stories Epics 3 to 8 v3.md (heading RWB-E5-018, its Endpoints table: POST cases and GET legal-actions); Recovery Workbench FSD S4 Litigation and enforcement v3 (A2.18.2 step 2 and step 3); Recovery Workbench TSD S4 Litigation and enforcement v2 (T-A.1 API-S4-004, T-A.2 PATCH); Template and Rules v1 R3 (source precedence)
section: APP s1 Story; s4 Flow step 10; s12.1; s13 Solution plan; s19 Out of scope; CON s3, s7 AC2, s12.1, s13
description: The legacy Endpoints table of RWB-E5-018 lists two operations, POST /cases/{caseId}/legal-actions and GET /legal-actions/{legalActionId}, while its own AC1 asks the firm to track the writ to execution and the FSD A2.18.2 step 2 has the actor enter or confirm values. The TSD S4 appendix T-A.1 declares API-S4-004 PATCH /legal-actions/{legalActionId} as the operation whose purpose is to record a filing, judgment or enforcement step, and T-A.2 gives its request, response and errors. Under the precedence of Template and Rules R3 the technical specification outranks the story master, so both slices declare three operations, the legacy Endpoints table is recorded as incomplete and the two legacy operation IDs are kept unchanged on the re-based paths.
evidence: The Endpoints table of RWB-E5-018 gives POST /api/recovery/v1/cases/{caseId}/legal-actions with Litigation C and GET /api/recovery/v1/legal-actions/{legalActionId} with Litigation R only. FSD S4 A2.18.2 gives the actor entering or confirming values in step 2 and the system recording the action in step 3. TSD S4 T-A.1 declares API-S4-004 PATCH /api/recovery/v1/legal-actions/{legalActionId} with Litigation U and First in E5, and T-A.2 gives its purpose as Record a filing, judgment or enforcement step.
owner_role: S4 rwb-litigation service owner with the solution architect
proposed: Declare the three operations of T-A.1, keep API-S4-002, API-S4-003 and API-S4-004 as the operation IDs, and let the story catalogue mark the legacy Endpoints table as incomplete for this key.
